  AGENDA STAFF REPORT

  DATE:  June 2, 2020

  TO:  Honorable Mayor and Members of the City Council

  APPROVED BY: Jose E. Ometeotl, City Manager

  PREPARED BY: Michelle G. Ramirez, Director of Community Development

  SUBJECT:  APPROVAL OF AN URGENCY ORDINANCE PROHIBITING THE SALE AND
  DISCHARGE OF SAFE AND SANE FIREWORKS WITHIN THE CITY OF LYNWOOD

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and adopt, by a 4/5th vote, the attached Urgency Ordinance (by
  title only) entitled “AN URGENCY ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD,
  COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 12-2 “FIREWORKS” OF
  THE LYNWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE, PROHIBITING THE SALE AND DISCHARGE OF SAFE AND
  SANE FIREWORKS WITHIN THE CITY OF LYNWOOD.”

  Background:

  State law provides cities with the authority to regulate and/or prohibit the sale of fireworks. (California Health and
  Safety Code § 12541). Since the City has the power to prohibit fireworks sales altogether, it also has the lesser
  power to impose reasonable conditions on the issuance of permits for the sale of fireworks (California Health and
  Safety Code §§ 12646, 12647).

  Applications for fireworks permits are accepted and reviewed in the City Clerk’s Office between March 1st and
  March 31st of each year and, soon thereafter, presented to the City Council for approval. The City allows up to
  fourteen (14) fireworks stands to operate between July 1 and July 4.

  The Lynwood Municipal Code (“LMC”) Chapter 12-2 “Fireworks” currently contains restrictions and requirements
  for the sale of “safe and sane” fireworks. Specifically, the LMC prohibits any person from selling fireworks without
  a special permit. The “safe and sane” fireworks are those fireworks identified by State law and the State Fire
  Marshal as being non-dangerous, and they include those fireworks typically purchased and used by private parties,
  not specially trained in fireworks, for Fourth of July fireworks demonstrations (see California Health and Safety
  Code §§ 12505, 12529).

  The sale and discharging of “safe and sane” fireworks would more than likely result in people congregating and
  abandoning social distancing requirements, which could potentially cause a spike in COVID-19 related cases.

City Council Special Meeting - Page 3 of 15
   Discussion and Analysis:

  The LMC allows the sale and discharge of “safe and sane” fireworks within the City limits for the Fourth of July
  holiday (LMC Chapter 12-2.4). By definition, “safe and sane” fireworks would include ground hand-held sparkling
  devices, cones, fountains, sparklers, ground spinners, snakes and smoke devices. Such activities as firework
  sales and discharging of fireworks on the Fourth of July holiday typically facilitate gatherings of more than a single
  household.

  The promotion of mass gatherings including individuals from more than one household would be inconsistent with
  public health orders and practices in place in the City at this time. Additionally, enforcing adequate social
  distancing at dispersed sites will likely be very difficult and would place a significant burden upon public safety
  resources that may be needed to respond to a potential second wave of COVID-19 cases. Therefore, it is
  recommended that the City Council adopt (by a 4/5ths vote) an urgency ordinance eliminating the sale and
  discharging of “safe and sane” fireworks.

  Fiscal Impact:

  There is no fiscal impact.

  City Manager's Officer

   URGENCY ORDINANCE NO.

  AN URGENCY ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF LYNWOOD, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES,
  STATE OF CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 12-2
  “FIREWORKS” OF THE LYNWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE,
  PROHIBITING THE SALE AND DISCHARGE OF SAFE
  AND SANE FIREWORKS WITHIN THE CITY OF LYNWOOD

  WHEREAS, pursuant to the California Emergency Services Act, Chapter 2-18 of
  the Lynwood Municipal Code, and Article XI, Section 7 of the California Constitution, on
  March 16, 2020, the City Council for the City of Lynwood held an “emergency” special
  meeting to update the local community on the COVID-19 crisis, and adopted a Resolution
  and Proclamation proclaiming a “local emergency,” allowing prompt response to
  emergency conditions at the local level, and providing the City access to federal, state,
  and local resources during the crisis; and

  WHEREAS, on May 5, 2020, the City Council reconsidered the conditions giving
  rise to the “local emergency” proclamation made on March 16, 2020, and determined that
  the conditions giving rise to the local emergency continue to exist, and extended the local
  emergency until July 17, 2020; and

  WHEREAS, on March 11, 2020, in order to slow the spread of COVID-19,
  Governor Newsom issued Executive Order No. N-25-20 prohibiting all California residents
  from gathering in groups larger than 250 persons; and

  WHEREAS, on May 26, 2020, the County of Los Angeles Department of Public
  Health Officer issued a revised order which prohibits gatherings of people who are not
  part of a single household or living unit, except for limited purposes, of which observing
  fireworks displays is not one; and

  WHEREAS, COVID-19 remains a contagious and potentially deadly virus that is
  spread by community transmission; and

  WHEREAS, the use or discharge of any fireworks, including “safe and sane”
  fireworks, encourages gatherings of people from different households in a single location;
  and

  WHEREAS, due to the economic impacts of COVID-19, the City of Lynwood does
  not possess the resources to enforce the gathering of persons from different households
  when people are gathered to observe fireworks, or that small groups of people maintain
  a safe distance from each other; and

  WHEREAS, the City of Lynwood does not possess the resources to enforce social
  distancing requirements at fireworks stands; and

  1
City Council Special Meeting - Page 5 of 15
   WHEREAS, the City Council further finds and declares that it is necessary and
  appropriate to adopt this Ordinance as an urgency measure, pursuant to Article XI,
  Section 7, of the California Constitution and Government Code Section 36937, given that
  fireworks are inherently dangerous; discouraging gatherings of persons is necessary to
  prevent the spread of COVID-19 and protect the public health and safety; the use of
  fireworks encourages crowds of people to gather together, especially on or around the
  Fourth of July; and the City of Lynwood does not possess the resources to otherwise limit
  the impacts on the health of Lynwood’s residents caused by failure to keep a safe distance
  at fireworks stands or fireworks displays, which justify adoption of this Ordinance as an
  urgency measure to be effective immediately upon adoption by a four-fifths vote of the
  City Council; and

  WHEREAS, all legal prerequisites to the adoption of this Ordinance have occurred,
  and the City Council has duly considered all evidence presented in connection with its
  consideration of this Ordinance.

  NOW, THEREFORE, THE CITY OF LYNWOOD CITY COUNCIL DOES
  ORDAIN AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. The facts set forth in the recitals of this Ordinance are true and correct, and
  incorporated into this Ordinance as substantive findings.

  Section 2. This Ordinance is adopted as an urgency measure pursuant to Government
  Code Section 36937 for the immediate preservation of the public health, safety, and
  welfare, and is adopted and justified based on the findings of the City Council in the
  Recitals of this Ordinance, which are supported by substantial evidence in the record
  associated with the City Council’s consideration hereof.

  Section 3. Chapter 12-2, “FIREWORKS,” of the City of Lynwood Municipal Code is
  hereby repealed in its entirety and replaced to read as follows:

  CHAPTER 12-2 – FIREWORKS

  12-2.1 Statement of Purpose:
  The purpose of this chapter is to protect the property of and provide for the health,
  welfare and safety of the citizens of Lynwood by prohibiting the possession, sale, use
  and discharge of any and all fireworks within the City of Lynwood.

  12-2.2 Definitions:
  “Dangerous fireworks” shall mean all fireworks other than SAS fireworks, and
  include, but are not limited to, those fireworks defined in Sections 12505 and 12561 of
  the California Health and Safety Code.

  “Person” shall mean any individual, person, firm, partnership, corporation,
  association or any other entity.

  2
City Council Special Meeting - Page 6 of 15
   “Safe and sane fireworks (‘SAS fireworks’)” shall mean only those fireworks
  which are defined in Section 12529 of the California Health and Safety Code and have
  been classified and registered as safe and sane by the state fire marshal.

  “Screaming fireworks” shall mean any SAS fireworks commonly known as a
  “Piccolo Pete,” “Screaming Willie,” “Whistle Pete,” “Whistling Phantom,” or any other
  SAS fireworks having the same appearance and discharge characteristics as any of
  these SAS fireworks.

  “State fireworks law” shall mean Section 12500 et seq., of the California Health
  and Safety Code.

  12-2.3 Restrictions on Possession, Sale or Discharge:
  It shall be unlawful for any person to:

  a. Possess, keep, store, use, discharge, ignite, explode, shoot, or set off any
  dangerous fireworks, SAS fireworks, or Screaming fireworks within the City of Lynwood;

  b. Sell, offer for sale, display for purposes of sale, or give away any dangerous
  fireworks, SAS fireworks, or Screaming fireworks within the City of Lynwood.

  12-2.4 Violations – Penalties:
  Any person who violates any provision of this Section shall be deemed guilty of
  a misdemeanor, and upon conviction thereof shall be punishable by the penalties and/or
  fines as provided for in Section 1-5 of this code, unless a specific fine for the violation
  is specified in this subSection.

  a. The fine for possession of dangerous fireworks, SAS fireworks, or Screaming
  Fireworks in the City is five thousand dollars ($5,000.00).

  b. The fine for discharging dangerous fireworks, SAS fireworks, and/or screaming
  fireworks in the City is five thousand dollars ($5,000.00).

  c. The fine for sale of dangerous fireworks, SAS fireworks, or Screaming
  fireworks in the City is five thousand dollars ($5,000.00).

  d. A person is guilty of a separate offense for each and every day or portion
  thereof during which he/she or it commits, continues, or permits a violation of this part.

  e. Nothing in this Ordinance shall be intended to limit any of the penalties
  provided for under the California Health and Safety Code or Penal Code with regard to
  the sale, use, possession, delivery, and/or transportation of Dangerous Fireworks.

  Section 4. If any Section, subSection, paragraph, sentence, clause, phrase, or portion
  thereof, of this Ordinance is declared by a court of competent jurisdiction to be
  unconstitutional or otherwise invalid, such decision shall not affect the validity of the

  Section 5. The City Council of the City of Lynwood hereby passes this Urgency

  Section 6. The City Clerk shall attest and certify to the adoption of this Ordinance and

  Section 7. This Ordinance shall go into effect and be in full force and effect immediately

  AGENDA STAFF REPORT

  DATE:  May 19, 2020

  TO:  Honorable Mayor and Members of the City Council

  APPROVED BY: Jose E. Ometeotl, City Manager

  PREPARED BY: Maria Quinonez, City Clerk
  Eduardo Sarmiento, Deputy City Clerk

  SUBJECT:  SALE OF SAFE AND SANE FIREWORKS

  Recommendation:

  Due to the unprecedented threat to public health and safety from COVID-19 Pandemic, staff recommends that the City Council review the
  agenda staff report, and approve staff recommendation to cancel the sale of Safe and Sane Fireworks until further notice in order to preserve the
  public health and safety of all Lynwood residents.

  Background:

  On March 4, 2020, Governor Gavin Newsom, declared a State of Emergency to exist in California as a result of the threat of COVID-
  19.

  Since then, The City of Lynwood has recommended a number of measures to be taken across the City to protect members of the public
  and City workers from an undue risk of contracting the COVID-19 virus. Our precautions over the past weeks and what we do over the
  next few weeks and possibly months will determine how well we overcome this emergency.

  On March 11, 2020, the World Health Organization characterized COVID-19 as a pandemic. The Centers for Disease Control and
  Prevention advises us that COVID-19 spreads easily from person to person and has issued guidelines recommending that the public
  adopt policies and routines to enable social distancing wherever possible.

  Here in the City of Lynwood, we must enhance our efforts to maintain good hand hygiene, making sure we’re covering our coughs and
  sneezes, and practicing social distancing. It is absolutely critical that we as a City do everything we can to slow the pace of community
  spread and avoid unnecessary strain on our hospitals and emergency responders. To aid in our efforts, under the emergency authorities
  vested in the Office of the City Council under the laws of the City of Lynwood, today the City Council orders that a series of temporary
  restrictions be placed on certain establishments and functions throughout our City in which large numbers of people tend to gather and
  remain in close proximity. The City Council of the City of Lynwood hereby declare the following orders this March 16, 2020 to be
  necessary for the protection of life and property of all Lynwood residents.

  Discussion and Analysis:

  With rare intermittent exceptions, the City of Lynwood has hosted an Annual Fourth of July Fireworks Show celebration at Lynwood City
  Park. Due to the unprecedented circumstances brought on by the COVID-19 pandemic, and the high threat to public health and safety
  the City of Lynwood has proactively taken steps to preserve the life and property of its residents.

  In order to preserve and continue the progress made in flattening the curve of illness caused by the COVID-19 pandemic in the state of
  California, the City of Lynwood continues to lead by example through its current executive order and Council actions. Therefore out of
  an abundance of caution the cancelation of the sale of Safe and Sane Fireworks until further notice will be considered by the City
  Council.
